critique_history.assessment:
- The aperture is an enormous circular horn, overwhelming the shell; replace it with a narrow, elongated volute opening along the body.
- The inflated body and aperture read as intersecting lobes rather than one continuous shell.
- Stripes wrap horizontally like bands; make them wavy longitudinal/radiating markings converging toward the spire.
- Refine the low spire into several broad, connected whorls without the pinched central depression.

- The body is boxy and vertically stretched; reshape it into a rounded, globular inflated whorl.
- The tall stacked spire contradicts the requested low spire; reduce it to a few broad, overlapping whorls.
- The aperture rim reads as a detached hoop; conform and embed it against the shell surface.
- Stripe boundaries are visibly pixelated; use a smooth procedural wavy brown-and-cream pattern.
